title: The Vineyard of Life and the Pit of Error
english: A sword, but it is shining. And the bow has been drawn and prepared to shoot the arrows of punishment, but it has not yet released the arrows, even though it has fashioned them and holds them ready to shoot. It can be said that instruments of death are prepared in a bow, those serving the punishments, often called instruments of wrath. For the wicked are not angels through whom wrath, anger, and tribulation are sent upon the worthy. And if even the fashioned arrows, having been filled with poisonous medicine, are instruments of death for those being punished, one must take heed.

He who has labored in iniquity has conceived pain to give birth to injustice (Ps 7:15–17). These are the offspring that the one who has conceived will bring forth in secret, he who is to be punished through iniquity and injustice which he did; and appropriately, he will seize both the pain in the punishment and the pain in the sinning. For the work of iniquity is most heavy and burdensome, compared to a talent of lead; for nothing is more inferior than evil, which always brings down the one who does it.

Some say that, because of the order of evil, the labor is spoken of before the seizing of the birth-pangs. For upon those pregnant, after the seizing, is the pain with which they give birth; but there, before the seizing, the pain is named because it lacks the rhythm and order of that in evil. And likewise the precedence of injustice over iniquity. For someone having become lawless from this, is not under the law of righteousness, so as to also set upon other men while he acts unjustly. This is found especially concerning Cain; for having become lawless by not rightly dividing what is due to God, he subsequently gave birth to injustice by attacking his brother lethally. Moreover, these voices belong especially to the devil, who is primeval-evil because he first acted lawlessly and unjustly. And every one sinning first harms himself, if he harms others; for the evil thing is injurious and harmful, first of all to the one participating in it, harming and damaging him. For the folly of a man defiles his ways, as it is said, 'the foolish will flee from evil' (Prov 14:16). Who is the pit into which the liar, who has done evil, will be cast? For it is written concerning a sinning soul, 'As a pit, so is Sheol' (Ps 183:4), just so.

Its wickedness is a pit. And often in the Scriptures, a pit is taken instead of wickedness, just as when the blind man leads the blind, both shall fall into a pit; and for this reason, blind teachers and students, who are under ignorance and other evils, must be avoided.

46 Having begun from hoping in the Lord his God, the Psalm settles into thanksgiving, as is fitting, having obtained the things requested or faithfully awaiting them; for 'I will confess' (Ps 7:18) declares thanksgiving here; therefore 'I will sing' is joined to it. And he confesses not as if by chance, but according to the righteousness of God; and he sings not aimlessly, but to the name of the Lord the Most High, as he declares having called Him to himself. Therefore also it is high according to holiness and virtue; for no lowly person, but only the one striving for piety, partakes of the Most High's approach.

47 For the life of every man is called a vineyard according to the Scriptures. Concerning such a thing, Naboth the righteous resisted the one demanding tyrannically, choosing rather to die than to give his vineyard to the one who wanted to make it a vegetable garden. For the man is magnanimous and the vineyard is unvanquished, a life most excellent, both practical and contemplative. The wicked desire to take this, not so that it may bear fruit according to its nature, but to tear it down into temporary and quickly withering things, vegetables appropriately named; for he says they will fall quickly like vegetables. This is said concerning those having temporary haste. Near to this vineyard are also those in the 'Aisma' of sins who are named in 'My mother's sons fought against me, they imprisoned me in vineyards; they did not protect my vineyard' (Ps 87:12).' We have passed over this, using only this expression to show for the sake of demonstration what the name of the vineyard signifies: life. He who bears clusters of truth and brings forth grapes through such a vineyard. Since the offspring of the vineyard have a season for being plucked, it is fitting to reap them and bring them into winepresses, so that they might make wine pressing that gladdens the heart of man. And since the life turns out to be both practical and contemplative, the former are the insights of truth, and the latter the work, which is praised for bearing fruit. And it is not one winepress upon which they are brought...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Exaltation of Christ and the Maturity of Believers
english: Not merely fruits, but more; for the ode is not for a single vintage, but for many vintages. Again, since the practical virtues are many fruits, each will have its own particular vintage; some bear fruits upon the vintage of temperance, those who succeed in chastity and maintain a pure bed; others bear fruits upon the vintage of courage, which those are the farmers of; and concerning the other virtues, they speak of similar things.

Since there are more vintages, those who farm the practical virtues bring them into them like the harvests of vineyards; it is necessary also that those who have borne the clusters of doctrines and theorems of truth bring more into them for the contemplative life. Having said these things, let no one neglect the following of the virtues. For they are one and of the same kind, but since those who partake do not have equal measure toward all, they possess [measure] from which they profit more than others; he who more fully partakes of justice is named from this, and likewise for each of the others. For you will likewise perceive the various beatitudes spoken in the Gospel, one being named from the most powerful grass, another from the merciful, and similarly regarding the rest.

But also in its own number, this ode is composed as the seventy-eighth. For it has much harmony with the resurrection day of the Lord, on which there has become a harvest of many vineyards, as the disciples of the Risen One are sent to make disciples of all nations and to testify to the Risen One to the ends of the earth, so that the proclamation of the Risen One may be spread everywhere, as it is immediately shown from the words of the psalm. 'Great is the name of the Lord in Israel' (Ps 73:2–3), which was said in former times when Israel alone was holding to godliness; but now, the prophecy having been fulfilled, 'all nations shall serve him' (Ps 22:27), (for he is the hope of the nations), 'Wonderful is your name become in all the earth' among those partaking of Christ's proclamation everywhere. For his name has been magnified over all, as it is carried in another psalm. And the cause of his name being wondered at throughout the earth is given in the following verse. For he says, 'Your majesty has been lifted up above the heavens,' so that you...

Having been taken up, rising from the dead, the Christians of the whole earth are called by your designation, O Christ. The majesty of the Savior is being praised; the economy, which received [its purpose] for the salvation of the world, is above the heavens. For what is it to find remaining in it lacking in greatness what is becoming? His majesty was lifted up above the heavens, having been made to sit at the right hand of Majesty in the high places after the cleansing of sins.

By this understanding, it must also be received that he has become higher than the heavens after the resurrection. But let not all those believing from the Gentiles and those coming to the Gospel from the circumcision—who, even if they should ever reach the age of a man, are infants in wickedness, being made infants through simplicity, not knowing evil—[be so]. The difference between infants and sucklings is shown from the word: those receiving milk are sucklings, while those having surpassed this age of infants are being called infants. It is appropriate, as the Apostle wrote to the Corinthians, 'I gave you milk, not food' (1 Cor 3:2). One must watch over this differently: the one being introduced, receiving milk, is a suckling; but the one having been perfected according to understanding, yet being an infant in wickedness, remains an infant. Such are all those having turned and having become like children.

For not much remains to them of having attained the knowledge of you, and of becoming like you in holiness and virtue, to take up as far as is possible (Ps 8:6). But most correctly he said, 'You made him a little lower than [the angels],' but 'You have not made him less [than the angels]' (Ps 8:5). For man, being equal and of equal strength to the immortal rational beings, was made lower than them by the providence of God, through which you alone, the one providing, having been surpassed by mortal life, were struck by the flesh. But even if it has not happened in that way regarding him, he has nonetheless been crowned with surpassing honor and glory by you, because he has become according to your image and likeness, through which image and likeness you have exercised the rational being, having subjected all things to him as being under his feet. title: The Judgment of Cities and the Error of the Jews
english: From here he brings in other words of the psalm. We see Jesus, who was made a little lower than the angels, being crowned with glory and honor through the suffering of death; for it was necessary for him, through whom all things and through whom all things, to lead many sons into glory, to perfect the leader of their salvation through sufferings (Ps 8:8–9).

Behold the sequence: it is not set to rule over all mortal creatures, but over the days (Ps 8:10). For the one-horned does not hold sway, nor does he stand against the others, strong and wild, as to rule the days, from the sheep and the ox and all the cattle of the field, and the following. I think this is not well said. For before these transgressions, man ruled; and the righteous rule even after these transgressions, as Daniel, having been thrown into the den of lions and suffering no harm from any of them, and Paul, having shaken off the viper from his own hand upon the fire. For wild beasts, they say, shall make peace with you; and in addition to these, the beasts of the field are included, as we have learned in Genesis.

It is fitting that the song spoken concerning the resurrection of the Savior should have a resemblance to the end at the beginning (Ps 8:10); for beginning and ending use the same words, the Spirit teaching the beginning to be the end according to the subject. It agrees with 'O Lord, how wonderful is your name in all the earth: let all the earth worship you and sing praises to you' (Ps 9:1).

Since it is not being defined who the Son is, what the Savior is is being made manifest in many ways by being so named. Indeed, in the Epistle to the Hebrews, Paul says, 'Christ, if he is a Son upon his own house, not we are' (Heb 1:8/2:13 context); and again, 'At the end of these days he spoke to us in a Son' (Heb 1:2); and the Savior himself writes about himself in the Gospel, 'If the Son does not set you free, you will be free indeed' (John 8:36). And also the proposed triumphal song has a reference to the end. For on account of that end, the Savior arrived, about which the precursor of the apostles writes: 'Having grasped the end of faith, the salvation of souls, concerning which salvation the prophets searched and inquired, and after a little time, testifying to the sufferings toward Christ...'

Regarding the glories that follow these things. Perhaps the Jews, concerning Absalom as the son of the one singing, will say that the inscription is true, being rebuked as they have not rightly received it, and because they are always in error for not searching the Scriptures. For what is it even plausible to say in the [work] 'On the Hidden Things', if they do not uncover the thoughts of Absalom that occurred in secret, [regarding] how the hidden things lie? And what is said by them possesses much elegance.

Such a sitting signifies him as a judge, but not that a certain seat has been established. Stand firm, if there is room to say, [that] after the nations have been rebuked, the impious shall perish in the manner of their ways, so as to no longer profit them. And this shall happen, the previously spoken thing being fulfilled thus: 'The way of the ungodly shall perish' (Ps 9:7a).

But the aggressions of the enemy are, in a sense, the heretical teachings and the vices according to appearance, which some have left as if they could no longer contend super-abundantly as cities, and they themselves shall be destroyed; for cities are collections of people standing together and being governed unlawfully. For it has been written concerning the one establishing them as 'building cities in vain and preparing cities in iniquity'. For their substance is wrongdoing and the shedding of blood of those being scandalized. The Savior, having arrived, pulls these down, pulling down the enemy who wishes to rule tyrannically, having been as it were cities.

Having seen this courage with divine eyes and speaking well, they say he is the best, as if uttering a gracious voice from one voice, beginning thus: 'Lord my God, I will glorify you, I will praise your name, what you have done wonderful things, an ancient and true counsel'; may it be, Lord, that what you have made cities into dust, a city of the ungodly, shall never be built for ever. Stand firm, if it signifies the raised ruin of Jerusalem, of the Savior having been crucified in it, of its citizens being the remainder of the ungodly because of the killing of the Lord (Ps 9:7b). 'The [structure] after the shout instead of with peace of those conquering has risen' (Ps 9:7b).
It exhorts the things set forth to withdraw indeed from wickedness and impiety, and to approach indeed virtue and piety (Ps 9:8b-9). For what mind, believing these things spoken thus, would not...
